utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Case number IT-01-47-T, The Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Could we have the appearances for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours, counsel and everyone in and around the courtroom. For the Prosecution, Daryl Mundis, assisted by Andres Vatter, our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, thank you. Could we have the appearances for Defence counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honours. For the Defence of General Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic, lead counsel, Stefane Bourgon, co-counsel, and Alexis Demirdjian, legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And could we have the appearances for the other Defence team, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Kubura, Rodney Dixon, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic and our legal assistant Nerman Mulalic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will now resume with the hearings on the 29th of March, 2005, after having had a UN holiday. Our witness has been waiting since Thursday. We will call him back into the courtroom. Could the usher please bring the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, General. Just before you entered the courtroom I was saying that we will now be resuming with your examination, I will take this opportunity to greet everyone present, Mr. Mundis, defence counsel, the accused, and everyone else in and around the courtroom. We will be continuing with the examination-in-chief. I think Mr. Bourgon concluded his examination-in-chief on Thursday so I will now give the floor to defence counsel for Mr. Kubura who will now be conducting their examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We will probably conclude our examination-in-chief by --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear Mr. Ibrisimovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could Mr. -- could General Karavelic have a look at his report, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: General, could you please have a look at the part of the report 476 to 479, paragraphs 476 to 479, which concern the 7th Muslim Brigade. In your report, you said that the 7th Muslim Brigade was established by order from the Supreme Command Staff on the 19th of November, 1992. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: In your report, you said that it was formed in the way that other brigades were formed. It was mobilised in the same way that other brigades were mobilised. It had similar or identical problems to those of other brigades. However, that's not what I'm interested in. That is already contained in the report that has been admitted into evidence. What I'm interested this is the following: When it was formed in November 1992, the brigade already had the title the 7th Muslim Brigade. That was the name of the brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says in the documents, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: So by order of the Supreme Command Staff that name was given to the brigade?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: General, on the basis of the documents that you reviewed, are you aware of the fact that brigades that had such names existed in other ABiH corps?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that. And in the course of the war, all ABiH corps had at least one Muslim brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether the 7th Muslim Brigade was the first one in the ABiH that was given that name, that was designated as the Muslim brigade, or was there some other such brigade in some other corps?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not certain, but I think that the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade was the first one that had such a name and it was formed in that way in the ABiH, although there were probably other smaller units in corps that perhaps had such a name, but I don't think there were any other brigades with such a name before.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: In your report, it says that the first such brigade with such a name was formed within the 5th Corps as the 101st Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's what it says in my report, then perhaps I have made a slip, because the report was drafted on the basis of the documents I had, so in that case it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Would you have a look at footnote 107 which is on page 73 of your report. Some brigades are referred to which were parts of other corps. The 1st Podrinje Muslim Brigade, the 243 Muslim Light Brigade, the 1st Muslim Mountain Brigade, the 17th Muslim Brigade, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything that is stated in the footnote is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: General, do you know whether such brigades, called Muslim brigades, existed as anti-fascist brigade in the course of the Second World War too?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, on the basis of the history I have studied, yes, such brigades did exist and were part of the coalition fighting against fascism. They were part of the anti-fascist coalition.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: A witness testified here, Professor Sehic, a professor of history, who in fact confirmed that and said that in the Second World War several brigades existed that were called Muslim brigades, and he mentioned the 16th Muslim Brigade which was the largest such brigade.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that is correct. And as far as I know, such units in the fight against fascism were very prominent units, units that had been remarked and that were much appreciated, if I may put it that way, by the political and military leadership and the anti-fascist coalition, and their contribution to the fight against fascism was immense.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: I would say that the tradition of such brigades was preserved after the Second World War within the framework of the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he is correct when he said that. According to what I know, that is correct. And all nations and peoples in the former Yugoslavia had the right to preserve their heritage and these traditions from the peoples' liberation war.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, you were the commander of the 1st Corps at one point in time in the course of the war. In the 1st Corps, was there a brigade that was called a Muslim brigade?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the 1st Corps of the ABiH, there was a plan to establish one such unit at least. However, for various reasons, we didn't succeed in doing so immediately. But this was only done at the beginning of 1994, and one such brigade was formed at that point in time which was part of the 1st Corps of the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you now clarify something for me: If there's an order from the Supreme Command Staff and the brigade is called the 7th Muslim Brigade or the 101st Muslim Brigade - it's not really important - can the brigade commander or anyone else influence the name? Can he have it changed if the command issues an order and says that the brigade should be given a certain name?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The brigade commander and people further up the chain of command can only make suggestions to change the name of a brigade. They can do nothing more. The Supreme Command gives brigades their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of the documents that you reviewed, Mr. Kubura arrived in 7th Muslim Brigade towards the end of December 1992, and at the beginning of 1993 he arrived there first as the assistant chief for operations and training. He later became the Chief of Staff. And when he was in that position, could he have had any influence, could he have suggested that the name of the brigade be changed?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can give you a broad answer. But very briefly my answer would be, no, he could have no influence on the name of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you this because Mr. Kubura arrived in the 7th Muslim Brigade when it had already been established by order from the Supreme Command Staff.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the documents you have, could you have a look at paragraph 477, in fact, in your report, where reference is made to Mr. Kubura. We know from the documents that he was first the assistant Chief of Staff, operations and training, in the December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what it says in the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: By order dated March 1993, Mr. Kubura became the Chief of Staff of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: In August 1993, Mr. Kubura became the commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, in the documents that you had at your disposal, did you find any reliable evidence or any facts or anything else pointing to whether Mr. Koricic, the commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade, left that brigade and went abroad?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In all the documents that I had at my disposal, and they're right behind me, and in many other documents that I had access to, I don't believe that I came across any document that referred to this subject among those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You didn't find a document that would say that this in fact happened on the 1st of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: General, in the documents that you saw, did you come across any evidence pointing to the fact that Mr. Kubura was authorised to represent the command of the 7th Muslim Brigade, Mr. Koricic? Is there any such document and did you come across such a document?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In accordance with my previous answer, I think that in this case too my answer would be the same. I didn't come across any documents that referred to him representing the commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: In the documents that you saw, did you come across any in which Asim Koricic was authorised by his superior command to be absent from the brigade?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I also -- I don't think that I saw any such documents either.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, on page 7, line 12, it should say Koricic, and according to the transcript it says Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: General, could you explain to us the procedure that is followed if Koricic was appointed as the brigade commander. When the brigade commander has to be absent for various reasons, what is the procedure that is followed in accordance with military regulations?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the service regulations of the JNA, or rather according to the provisions of those regulations that were adopted by the ABiH, I think that when it's not possible for the brigade commander to perform his duties, when it's not possible for any brigade commander to perform his duties, the superior is duty-bound to draft a document, or rather an order, in which the next person in the chain of command is designated as the commander or perhaps some other officer so that this officer can perform those duties for a certain period of time. I think that if the period of time is a two-month period, then the deputy or Chief of Staff has to perform those duties, if the deputy isn't present, and it's not even necessary to draft any orders with regard to that matter. However, if the period of time is over two months, then the superior is duty-bound to draft an order on representing the brigade commander for a certain period of time. Up to six months at the most. This period of time can be up to six months at the most. But the superior can extend this six-month period of time for another six months. But only on one occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, to facilitate this and to obtain some clarifications from the General, I would like the witness to have a look at document P243. We have a sufficient number of copies for everyone here. This is P243. It's a decree of law on the ABiH dated the 1st of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: General, have a look at Article 78, please of this decree.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's page 17 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Have you found Article 78?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: It says that an officer who is temporarily unable to perform his duties is a signed representative.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 3, it says being represented in accordance with one and two can -- Article 1 and 2 can go on for about six months and, if another officer takes such a decision, this period of time can be extended to one year from the date on which the duty is assumed, or such duties are assumed. That means that the Superior Command has to regulate this matter by issuing an order on representing a commander if the commander of the unit is absent. In this case, we're referring to brigade commander. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that that is quite correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: In the same article it says that this period of time can be extended for another six months and in accordance with an order from a superior officer, from a Supreme Command Staff. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: When reviewing these documents, you didn't come across an order regulating the situation had he Mr. Koricic left the brigade and when Mr. Kubura was appointed as the representative of the brigade commander in accordance with an order that had been issued?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that I didn't come across any such documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Let's just clarify something. You didn't find a document stating that Mr. Koricic was authorised to be absent from the brigade and you didn't come across any documents in which an order was issued stating that Mr. Kubura would be representing the brigade commander, nor did you come across any documents stating when Mr. Koricic left the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's quite correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Please have a look at, in the same series of documents, the rules of service in the ABiH, Article 14. In the Bosnian version it's page 50; in the English version, it's page 39. It says that if a unit -- it refers to cases when units are suddenly left without a superior officer. General, have you found the article?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: "If a unit is left without a superior officer," have you found that?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you just clarify the following situation: If a unit is suddenly left without a commander, there's a situation when units suddenly -- is suddenly left without a commander. For example, a commander dies or is killed.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this article refers to extraordinary circumstances, if the brigade commander is killed or dies or if he is captured, et cetera. So it concerns unexpected events. And then the second person in the chain of command has the duty to assume the duties of the brigade Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. commander, or rather he has to command with the brigade. He has to continue commanding the brigade. But the superior has to regulate this situation by issuing an order as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: But this does not concern the situation that existed between Mr. Koricic and Mr. Kubura in the 7th Muslim Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to place that within the context of this article.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And now when we see that Mr. Kubura was first assistant commander for operations and training and then an order was issued in March pursuant to which he was appointed the Chief of Staff, and in the indictment it is stated that Mr. Kubura represented a commander as of the 1st of April. My question to you is as follows: Would it be possible for anybody to perform the same -- the two sets of duties in the same brigade at the same time?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I was studying documents, I also looked at the order pursuant to which Amid Kubura was appointed the Chief of Staff at the same time he was the deputy commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade. Pursuant to that order, Brigadier Kubura had already been given two duties to perform, irrespective of the fact that they may be integrated, conditionally speaking, into one position or one set of duties. Any further assignments, building on an already existing, complicated position in my view is unacceptable for the following reason: If somebody performs the duties of the commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade and, if it was Brigadier Kubura, that means that he had three sets of duties, which is unacceptable, according to any principles of or doctrines of any of the militaries of the world.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. As you were studying this documentation, you saw that Mr. Kubura did not have any idea as to when Mr. Koricic might return to the brigade?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't come across any sources that would confirm that he did have any knowledge as to that fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: His status as an officer in the 7th Muslim Brigade was finally resolved when he was appointed a commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade which was on the 6th of August, 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In legal terms, this would be the date when he was factually appointed the commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade. However, at the same time, this is the moment when the new Chief of Staff was appointed as well as the deputy commander and other officers. Pursuant to this particular order, he was appointed a commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade, but he was also relieved of his former duties of the Chief of Staff and the deputy commander of that brigade, and this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: This is precisely what I was going to ask you. Mr. Kubura was the Chief of Staff until the 6th of August, 1993 when he was appointed the commander of the 7th Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my point of view, I believe that this is exactly what happened. And as I'm looking at the situation from the point of view of legal aspects, I would say that this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: At the moment when the brigade was given a new commander, when the new commander was appointed, and that was in August 1993, wasn't Mr. Kubura in the position to take the brigade over from somebody else should there have been a handover from some previous commander?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under all -- any circumstances, the answer would be yes, unless the previous commander was either killed or captured.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: And now I would like to ask you about the events in the villages of Miletici and Maline. Could you please look at paragraph 691 of your expert report. When it comes to Miletici, you said that you didn't find any documents or evidence that would point to the presence of the 7th Muslim Brigade on that particular day in Miletici, hence there is no responsibility on the part of Mr. Kubura for the events in Miletici, and you agreed with Mr. Reinhardt who confirmed that.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This may be seen in my paragraph 691. I have not come across any relevant documents that would speak to the contrary.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did you find any documents among the documents that you studied, pointing to the fact that the 7th Muslim Brigade or its command or the battalion in Travnik requested any report on the events in Milici in 1993?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at paragraph 721 of your report. When it comes to the village of Maline, my question is the same: Among the documents that you studied, did you find any evidence pointing to the fact that the 7th Muslim Brigade was in Maline in June 1993?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like in the previous case, the -- my answer is the same. I did not find any relevant documents pointing to that fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Your position is identical as the position of the military expert Mr. Reinhardt who says that he did not find any relevant documents pointing to the presence of the 7th Muslim Brigade on that particular day in the village of Maline?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did you find any documents pointing to the fact that the 7th Muslim Brigade, its command or its battalions are requested to send any reports on the events in Maline in June 1993?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. General, can we please move on to the part of your report talking about the events in Vares in November 1993 starting with paragraph 833 of your report. I will not repeat your words. Could you please look at paragraph 834 and your conclusion with regard to the responsibility of Mr. Kubura, with regard to the events in Vares in 1993. You're saying that he did everything else -- everything possible to prevent his subordinates from plundering?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is what it says in paragraph 848.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: As you were studying the documents that you had at your disposal, did you also study the report sent by General Alagic dated 8 November 1993. This is P449 in which it says as follows: "The plunder by all of the formations that were present was prevented by the urgent intervention of the OG East of the 7th Muslim Brigade and the Ministry of the Interior." [As interpreted]

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I read this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Does this document point to the fact that the 7th Muslim Brigade did their utmost to prevent plundering in November 1993 in Vares?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did you take into account the report by General Divjak dated 17th of November, 1993? This is P450. I repeat the date is 17 November 1993, although in the documents that you have it is obvious that the 7th Muslim Brigade left Vares much earlier. In this report it says as follows: The units of the second corps are in Vares, about 300 troops are there. And individual plunder in Vares started once these units entered the town of Vares. And this report was sent to the 3rd Corps for their information.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I read this document and I'm aware of its contents, and I believe that this is the truth of the matter, if I may say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, on line -- on page 14, line 21, it should read: "OG Bosanska Krajina and military police and the 7th Muslim Brigade." This is just for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Finally I would like to ask you, General: Do you know Mr. Kubura?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Were you his superior at any point in time?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was his second in command.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any dealings with Mr. Kubura at that time?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was the -- one of the commanders on the strength of the 1st Corps. He was the commander of the 1st Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: And what experiences did you have with Mr. Kubura? How did you perceive him at the time?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise that I will maybe sound subjective. This is not any kind of bias on my part, but I would like to say that he is a man who has a lot of military experience; a man who has very high moral standards and moral integrity; a man who makes a distinction between the good and the evil; he is a patriot; he has a very broad understanding of society and all the problems in Bosnia-Herzegovina. I'm saying this on purpose because Bosnia-Herzegovina is a very complex society. He always had very correct and very proper views of the society of Bosnia-Herzegovina and Bosnia-Herzegovina as an entity. He was a very diligent, very hard working person. And so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: And what about the unit that was under his command in the 1st Corps?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say only this: I should only have been so lucky to have established that unit even sooner.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we don't have any more questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to give the floor to the Prosecution for their cross-examination. Cross-examination by Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, General.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: For the record, sir, my name is Daryl Mundis and along with my colleagues here today we represent the Prosecution in this case. I have two other points I would simply like to clarify with you before I begin. And the first is, sir, we did briefly meet when you testified in the Galic case for the Prosecution. I don't know if you remember, but I was in fact one of the Prosecutors in that case and we did, on that occasion, meet very briefly in Mr. Stamp's office. And I would also like to draw your attention to the fact that I believe it was in the early summer of 2004, pursuant to an order of the Trial Chamber, that the Prosecution call some additional witnesses in this case. I did speak with you briefly on the telephone at which point in time you informed me that you had been approached by Madam Residovic, and we then terminated that phone conversation. But I just wanted to put that on the record. Before I commence with my questioning, sir, I would simply like to indicate to you that my intention is not in any way to confuse you. And if you don't understand any of the questions that I ask you, please feel free to tell me that and I will rephrase the question so that you understand exactly what it is that I'm asking you. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, I take it from the comments that you told the Presiding Judge when you first began testifying more than a week ago that this is actually the first time you've testified as an expert witness. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And General, just to avoid any confusion, when you testified for the Prosecution in the Galic case, you were testifying as a fact witness, that is, to things that you observed or things that you did as the 1st Corps commander. You were not testifying as an expert in that case.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would like to focus first, sir, on the methodology, that is, the means by which you produced the report that we have before us in the current proceedings. I believe in paragraph 8 of your report, you indicated that you were first approached by the Defence for General Hadzihasanovic in May 2004. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And you were still at that point in time on active duty in the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, at what point in time do you consider -- or were you actually retained by the Defence for General Hadzihasanovic? That is, when did you first agree to undertake this assignment as an expert?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already answered that. In legal terms I was still a member of the BiH army, although my retirement was already in the pipeline and it was just a matter of procedure and formality when I would stop wearing the uniform. And this is just an addition to my previous answer. And after the initial contacts in May 2004, very soon after that, at a second meeting, I confirmed to Mrs. Residovic that I would, indeed, take on the challenge.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, approximately when was that second meeting where you agreed to take on the challenge?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very soon. Maybe 10 or 15 days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So that was either also in May 2004 or sometime in early June 2004, to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, let's say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what, sir, was your official retirement date from the army?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the documents, it was on the 31st of August, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, at the time that you accepted, as you put it, the challenge -- and I know how much work goes into producing these reports, at the time you accepted this assignment or challenge to serve as an expert for the Defence, did you, in your mind, have any doubt as to the innocence of the two accused in this case?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would sooner say that I did not have any doubts, but I can't actually say either yes or no, because I did have certain doubts. My position was rather neutral. I accepted this challenge because I wanted to see what I would come across and, through my hard work and through my analysis of the documents, I came up with my expert report. I don't know to this very day whether these two are guilty or not. I'm just trying to show you through the documents and to explain to the Trial Chamber the military steps and the military actions, the actions and steps of a commander in the given circumstances that prevailed at the time. I'm trying to explain why things were done in a certain way and not in another way, whether things should have been done in that particular way, and how things were being done at that time, without any documents, without any orders, because they were just done as a result of the situation that prevailed at any given moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: General, at paragraph 8 of your report, you write that you were asked to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would kindly ask the witness to repeat the beginning of his answer, which is on page 16, line 13. It would be very good for the witness to repeat the answer in his own language, because the answer did not come out very clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, could you please repeat your question. Could you maybe rephrase it? Can you put it in such a way so as to avoid any confusion? This question is on page 16, line 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, just the very beginning of the witness's answer, the rest is clear. However, the first two sentences, I don't think that what is recorded in the transcript really represents what he said in his own language.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, page 16, line 13, according to the English transcript, is Mr. Ibrisimovic's direct examination. I'm not sure exactly what question, if it's simply the previous question...

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. President. My LiveNote was a bit delayed, so I don't have the same page number and the same line number. It is page ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If it is simply the preceding question, I can Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. certainly rephrase that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: General, let's go back to the question you had just answered and let me try this in a slightly different way. At the time you began or you were retained to produce your expert report, did you have any beliefs with respect to whether the two accused in this case were guilty or innocent of the charges in the indictment?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I'm more confused by this question than I was by your previous one. I was informed of the main elements and facts of the indictment. However, I did not give myself the right, nor did anybody ask me to do that, nobody ever instructed me as to whether I should form an opinion of their responsibility. And my answer would be that I took on this challenge to see, since my retirement was already in the pipeline and I was supposed to leave the BiH army and this was a transition period for me and this was a new engagement, something that would fill that transition period. And this gave me an opportunity to see what it was like to be an expert. I just was curious to see what I would come across. I came across a host of documents, and based on all these documents and my conversations with some other professionals, I drafted my report, and my answer would continue along the lines of the answer already given to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you a couple of follow-on questions, sir. Page 21, line 4 you say: "I was informed of the main elements and facts of the indictment." And my question to you, sir, is, at any point in time while you've been engaged in this process of producing and writing your report, did you actually read the full text of the indictment against the two accused?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, you write at paragraph 8 in your report that you were asked to replace another former ABiH general who had been retained by the Defence in 2002, but who was no longer available due to personal reasons. Again, this comes from paragraph 8 of your report.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, the name of your former colleague that was initially retained and whom you replaced?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Sead Delic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And sir in paragraph 10 of your report, you indicate that you requested to meet with the former military expert. Before I get to that I believe the transcript, line 6, page 22, it says General Sad Gailic. Can you please spell the name of the initial expert retained by the Defence for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: S-e-a-d D-e-l-i-c.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, sir, let's turn to paragraph 10 of your report where you state that you requested to meet with the former military expert, Sead Delic who had been retained by the defence. My first question is: Did in fact you meet with General Sead Delic?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did meet with him. I saw him or had contact with him on a number of occasions. And he had already done some of the work, in terms of taking or gathering correct information from the census, the population census, from 1990, and I came across a lot of errors, as I had to do that part of the work again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, General, you said you met with him on a number of occasions. Can you give us a rough approximation as to how many times you met with General Sead Delic?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that we saw each other about twice, and we spoke to each other over the phone between five and ten times.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, --

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I even asked him to bring me his book, which he brought to my office later on, a book that he had published two or three years before then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, the title of that book or the subject matter of that book?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That book was, in fact, his master thesis that he defended at the university of political science, the faculty of political science. And the title of the book -- or the book was in fact about the role of all international bodies that were present in Bosnia and Herzegovina in the course of the war. And I can't remember the title of the book now, but I do have it at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, at the time -- in mid-2004 when you took over this assignment from General Sead Delic, had he commenced drafting a report?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Part of it, yes. I'd say that he had started working on a minor part of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And as part of your preparations for taking over this assignment, did he provide you with his -- the part that he had written? Or did you read it or review it, or in any way incorporate his work into this report that you've produced?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But because the questions were subsequently amended, most of what he had done was just irrelevant. And there was a very small part that had to do mostly with the calculating of the movement of a population in Central Bosnia. This is the part that I used to a certain extent, although I had to make certain changes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me turn now, sir, to paragraph 15 of your report in which you state that the cut-off date for new material that you reviewed was 17 December 2004. I simply want to clarify with you whether you reviewed any of the trial transcripts or exhibits that were admitted after the 17th of December 2004.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking me whether I had a look at such documents or rather whether I read such documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'm asking you, sir, let me be more precise. I'm asking you whether you relied on any of the testimony that was given after the 17th of December, 2004, or you relied on any of the documents that were admitted into evidence after 17 December 2004 in producing the report.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read most of the transcript of the military expert, General Reinhardt. I read quite a large part of the transcripts of the -- the testimony of certain witnesses. I'm not sure whether that was up until the 17th of December or after the 17th of December. I couldn't provide you with a precise answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you this then, sir. In paragraph 15 of your report, you indicate that the cut-off date for new material that you reviewed was 17 December 2004. And my question is, if that statement, in paragraph 15, which you also referred to in paragraph 21, you refer to 17 December December 2004 -- if in fact that was the cut-off date for the material that you reviewed. Whether you read the material after that date or not is a different question. But my question is, the evidence that was presented up until the 17th of December, 2004 seems to be what you're telling us is the cut-off date.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. I also read the summary reports of witnesses after the 17th of December, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me ask you this: With respect -- and again you might want to note in paragraph 21 of your report, you make reference to the testimony of 98 Prosecution witnesses and 26 Defence witnesses. And my question, sir, is: Did you read the transcripts of the testimony of those 98 Prosecution witnesses and 26 Defence witnesses?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read in detail Reinhardt's five-day report. And, as I have just said, I read summary reports, the most important parts that had been extracted from the witnesses' testimony. But I did not read in detail transcripts of the testimony of all the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And these summary reports, who produced them?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The office -- Mrs. Residovic's office, I believe, and Mr. Ibrisimovic's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: With respect to General Reinhardt's five-day testimony, you read the full transcripts of those five days?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And there were about 150 pages of that testimony, I think. From Monday to Friday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, what language were the transcripts, these 150 pages, what language did you read them in?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read General Reinhardt's testimony, or the transcript of his testimony in English, whereas I read the testimony of other witnesses in the Bosnian language.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, when you say "I read the testimony of other witnesses in the Bosnian language", are you talking about the summaries that were produced by the attorneys for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's probably what it was. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I note the time. This might be an appropriate spot for the first technical break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll have our technical break now. It's 3.30. We will resume at about five to 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: General Karavelic, before the break we were talking about the transcript and summaries of testimony that you reviewed in preparing your report and I do have a few follow-up questions, just so that we're clear as to what testimony or transcripts you looked at. You told us, sir, that you read the trial transcripts of the Prosecution expert General Klaus Reinhardt and other than that you read summaries. And my question, sir, is: Other than General Reinhardt's testimony, transcript testimony, did you read the full transcripts of any of the other witnesses, whether Prosecution or Defence?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't read the full transcripts of the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, these summaries, can you tell us approximately how long the summaries were of the witnesses that you did review?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, altogether the transcripts consisted of about 100 or 150 pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, when you use the word "transcript" - or at least it's translated to me as "transcript" - are you talking now about the summaries that were produced by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the original transcript, such as in the case of General Reinhardt. I'm referring to the summaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So the summaries produced by the Defence of the 98 Prosecution witnesses and 26 Defence witnesses ran to about 100 or 150 pages of summarised testimony. Is that your recollection?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned a number, but I can't really confirm that, because there were a lot of documents that I read and then there were these documents that have been registered. I read them over a long period of time, but there were a lot of pages. There was a lot of material that related to the summaries. I read a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But again you told us that the summaries were 100 to 150 pages, is that, to the best of your recollection, how much material you read with respect to these summaries?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that would be my assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You told us, sir, that the summaries were produced by the attorneys. Do you have any further elaboration as to who produced these summaries or how -- for example, who gave them to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know who made them. All I know is that I read them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. The witness never said the summaries were prepared by the Defence. I would like that to be clear for the transcript. They weren't prepared by Defence counsel. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, you have heard what Defence counsel has just said. They said that Defence counsel did not prepare the summaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If you give me a moment, Mr. President, I believe the witness said they were prepared by the advocates. I asked him -- again, my transcript is -- the time 15:28:31 seconds. I asked these summary reports, who produced them. And the witness's answer was: "The office, Mrs. Residovic's office, I believe, and Mr. Ibrisimovic's office." But I will ask a follow up question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You've said, sir, that you don't know who produced the summaries; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Who gave you the summaries?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I received them in the office, from the team.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when you say "in the office," what office are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to Mrs. Residovic's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, when you say "from the team", who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To a number of individuals working on General Mustafa Polutak [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And General Mustafa Polutak was or is an investigator working for the Defence team of General Hadzihasanovic; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't confirm that. I had contact with him, but as to what he does, I don't know. I assume that that is the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, where did you physically prepare this report and review these documents? Did you work from an office at home? Where did you physically produce this report and review the numerous documents?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly I worked at home with my assistants and I would go to Mrs. Residovic's office as well, most frequently, and I would spend days reading documents that they gave to me. And I spent less time in Mr. Ibrisimovic's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me return for a moment to the testimony, the trial transcript evidence of General Klaus Reinhardt. But before I do that, sir, let me ask you this: You told us on the first day of your testimony that among the different courses you attend were some that were held in Garmish; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And those courses in Garmish in Germany were at the George C. Marshall Center run by the United States Armed Forces; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you at any point in time, while you were a student at the George C. Marshall Center in Garmish, meet General Klaus Reinhardt?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether I did, but that's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, earlier, sir, you told us that - and this was at 1529 hours earlier this afternoon - there were about 150 pages of that testimony, referring to General Reinhardt's five-day testimony. Are you sure that it was 150 pages?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd sooner say there were far more pages, but the number of pages was about identical to the number of pages that my report has -- or rather about twice as long as my report. I'd say though far more pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, because I checked during the break, sir, and General Reinhardt's testimony -- which occurred from 3 through 7 May 2004 in English runs to 544 pages. Is it possible, sir, that you read 544 pages of testimony of General Reinhardt, in English?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my previous answer, I was thinking of one binder, but in fact there were two. In one binder there was three days of his testimony, and in the other binder, two days of his testimony. And I read most of it, not to say 100 percent.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's return, sir, to the summaries of the other witnesses. Do you recall, sir, or do any names stick out in your memory as to any of the other witnesses who testified and whose summary of evidence you recall reading?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps before you answer that, Mr. President we might want to go into private session in the event that any of the witnesses were protected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Registrar, let's go Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At home I read about the Sefer Halilovic case, because of my possible engagement in that case. And I was sitting at my computer and I was following the entire case, and I would download those things that could be downloaded. I was also reading papers every day, and I cut out those articles that referred to the work of the Tribunal. I compiled all of that and I came up with my expert report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, General, you've made reference to the Halilovic case, and my question is focussed precisely on this trial, that is the case against General Enver Hadzihasanovic and Brigadier Amir Kubura. Did you also follow these court proceedings on the Internet? Did you listen to or observe or watch witness testimony being broadcast over the Internet in this trial?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only partly. Not all of this. Not all of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you recall or give us more specifics as to how frequently you watched these proceedings and/or which witnesses testified or which events were being described during the time periods you followed the proceedings over the Internet?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, it's very difficult for me to give you a precise answer. When I log on my computer, the connection breaks up. By the time I log on again, I get a different witness. My computer is very slow. And it was my -- I derived satisfaction from following these cases. And I also wanted to do it for several reasons, for a number of reasons, and I really wouldn't be able to give you any exact number. I might be mistaken. I can't rely on my memory for that, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: With respect to the frequency, sir, can you tell us on average, did you follow the proceedings once a day, once a week, once a month? Were there certain proceedings that you followed more intensely than others?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In very simple terms, I log on and whatever happens, I follow it. I just come across things that are on-line at the time and I read things, I listen to things, that's what I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall or do you have a list of any of the documents that you downloaded from the Internet with respect to this case?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to go back home. I would have to look at all the papers that still remain that have not been destroyed or shredded in the meantime, and only then would I be able to give you a more precise answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: General, I would like to turn now to the exhibits and other documents that you have reviewed. If you could please turn to paragraphs 21 and 22 of your report, I have a few questions. In paragraph 21, you make reference to 939 exhibits introduced by the Prosecution, more than 1.640 exhibits presented by the Defence for General Hadzihasanovic and 26 exhibits presented by the Defence for Brigadier Amir Kubura. And in paragraph 22 you say: "I have read all of the above material, from which I selected that which I found to be relevant to the issues which I was asked to address." And my question, sir, is: Did you read all of these exhibits as described in paragraph 21? Or did you review them and only read those which you believed were most important?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would really like to be very precise in my answer; however, my answer would be, yes, I read most of it. I read two-thirds of it. Some of the things I just reviewed, I skimmed through, as I believed that this was not important. But I can't tell you exactly how much of that material I only reviewed. It's impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: In undertaking, sir, the exercise with respect to these exhibits, did anyone in any way suggest to you which exhibits were more important than others, or did anyone assist you in prioritising these exhibits? Than others? Or did anyone assist you in prioritising these exhibits?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was told how many documents there were presented by either the Defence or the Prosecution and I was told that I was supposed to read all of these documents. And it was up to me to read all of them, after having been faced with the questions that I was supposed to answer. It was up to me to decide whether some of them were relevant or not. I had my own way of prioritising documents which I focussed on in the light of some particular questions. For example, I singled out some seven or eight documents issued by the Republika Srpska army or by the HVO, just by way of example, which sent each of the documents and directly cooperated in terms of assisting each other with logistics, with artillery support, with taking over each other's lines and so on and so forth. I can even tell you which documents I am referring to when they were produced when they can be located. This is the type of lists I had when I was drafting my report. This is the way I singled out some of the documents for which I deemed that they were of relevance for my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But just so we're clear then, General, you personally determined which documents were important and which weren't. No one assisted you in identifying or prioritising the exhibits that you were provided with?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have anybody working directly on that. However, I had contacts with some people that I worked with and some of them would, from time to time, draw my attention to a particular document that they believed was of particular importance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, can you tell us who these people were that you worked with who would from time to time draw your attention to particular documents? Who were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, the answer is the same as was -- to one of your previous questions, the person in question is General Mustafa Polutak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Other than General Mustafa Polutak, did anyone else draw your attention to any particular documents from among the exhibits that you were provided with?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had a lot of conversations with Mrs. Residovic, Mr. Ibrisimovic, Mr. Bourgon. However, I can't pinpoint anything and say that anything was of particular importance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me move on to a slightly different but related subject, which is also set forth in paragraph 21 of your report. You state: "I have also relied on proposed exhibits by the Defence for General Enver Hadzihasanovic and the Defence for Brigadier Amir Kubura." And my question to you, sir, is: Do you have a list of the proposed exhibits that you relied upon in producing your report?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the list of these documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, let me try to rephrase this. Sir, in paragraph 21 of your report you make a distinction between the 939 exhibits introduced by the Prosecution, the more than 1640 exhibits presented by the Defence for General Hadzihasanovic and 26 exhibits presented by the Defence for Brigadier Amir Kubura and then go on to say: "In addition, I have also relied on proposed exhibits by the Defence for both accused." And my question is: With respect to the proposed exhibits, do you have a list of those documents that you relied upon in producing this report?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I cannot be precise in my answer. I know that we spoke about these documents, but I can't give you their list. I don't have such a list. And for these documents here, all of them, the three figures that you have mentioned, I have a list of those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So that we're clear then, you have a list of the exhibits up until 17 December 2004 that you relied upon in producing your report, but you do not have a list of other proposed exhibits that were provided to you and which you relied upon in producing your report; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less correct. I did talk about some documents that could be called or that could fall into that category. However, I can't confirm that these were those documents. I don't have a list of these documents nor do I know whether they have been tendered into evidence. I don't have such a confirmation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: General, do you have a list of all the documents that you reviewed or read in producing this report? Do you have like a master list of all the documents that you looked at, whether they were provided to you, or whether you downloaded them, or whether you clipped them out of a newspaper? Do you have any such master list of the material that you relied on in producing this report?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The documents that I am pointing to at the moment -- and let me be clear: All the documents that were registered with the court and which were represented by any of the sides, I have a list of those documents. As for the other things which were the product of my resourcefulness, my downloading them or cutting them out or obtaining them from any other source, no, I don't have such a list. I never compiled such a list. In my footnotes, you can find the additional things that I used. I believe that my footnotes may partially answer your question. However, besides the documents that are behind me and the footnotes, I don't have any other lists of the documents that I used for my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me turn now, sir, to the assistance that you received in producing this report. You told us, on Monday of last week, that is the 21st of March, 2005, page 44, lines 4 through 11, that you relied upon three assistants. You indicated a typist, someone who helped you with computer graphics, and it's unclear from the transcript what role was played by the third person. And I'm wondering if you can tell us what type of assistance the third person provided to you.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The key personnel was the guy called Faris Fadzan, who was in charge of my annexes or, in other words, he was in charge of computer work, because I am not very well versed in computers. The second person -- do you want names? The second person was the typist, but it was not always the same person. For the most part, it was one person. And the third person was the person who drew up all the topographic maps. That was the person who drew up topographic maps using geographic maps, not the computer. It was not the computer plotting of topographic maps. Their names are Faris Fadzan, Alma Kadric, and Midhat Sarac. Midhat Sarac is an expert for drawing topographic maps. Faris Fadzan is an expert in IT, and Alma Kadric, who was my typist throughout most of my work.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And can you tell us, sir, who these three individuals were employed by in assisting you in these capacities?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I employed them. Because within of them is also retired and the other two worked outside their working hours mostly during the weekends.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now sir also on the 21st of March 2005, that is the first day of your testimony a week ago yesterday, page 44, lines 9 through 11, you said: "I also received a lot of assistance from many other individuals in terms of using documents from the archives of the federation army, et cetera, et cetera." Can you elaborate upon that answer that you gave? What did you mean by "using documents from the archives of the federation army"?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me give you an example. I wanted on two or three occasions to look at the zones of responsibility of various corps and how they changed over time. And this could not be found on any of the existing maps. Then I asked for some topographic maps from the archives of the BiH army and I did that through General Polutak. I consulted these topographic maps and, after that, I used the information that I obtained from those topographic maps in order to compile my annexes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, other than topographic maps, did you make any requests for Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. documents from archives of the ABiH or from any other Bosnian government archives?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not request any particular documents. Mustafa Polutak was the one who had the list of documents that were registered with the Tribunal. And I did not find it necessary. For example, when it comes to the questions put to me by Mr. Ibrisimovic, I asked -- I was asked whether there was an order for the replacement or appointment of Brigadier Kubura. And my answer was there isn't. On some occasions I double-checked that with some other persons. I received the same answer, and I was able to close the door on such a particular question. I did not need to look any further. I had my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And when you say that you double-checked information with other persons, can you tell us, if you recall, the identity of any of these persons and where they were employed?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most often those were people who were retired a long time ago, or recently I also spoke to some of the active servicemen and so on and so forth. I would ask them whether this or that brigade was really established at a certain time or was it just something that existed on paper. This is more or less the subjects that I discussed with them. For example, I would ask them what the situation was in Vitez in June 1993. I'm just giving you examples. I had such conversations with people, but these conversations were simply my conversations with these people, and I cannot use their names to tell you this or that person told me this or that. However, based on the -- these conversations and all the things that we have mentioned, I was able to compile my expert report that I totally stand by.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are now in open session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you now, sir, about the specific assignment that you received in producing this report. Again, a week ago yesterday on the 21st of March, 2005, at page 47, lines 10 through 13, you told us that shortly after you accepted this assignment, you were provided with the first version of the questions that you were asked to answer. Do you remember testifying about that eight days ago?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, I believe you've told us earlier this afternoon that you accepted this assignment to produce this report some time in May or June 2004; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you give us a rough approximation of the time period that you received the first version of the questions that the Defence asked you to answer?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could put it in my own words. After I accepted this challenge, I was immediately presented with a draft of the questions and of the chapters that my predecessor, General Sead Delic, had already formulated to a certain extent. However, at the same time I was immediately told that there would be corrections. But I was told there was a lot of material, a lot of questions that would not be changed, and I was told that I could start working immediately, which I did. I can't say when exactly, but in two cases, and to a certain extent in the third case too, questions were amended in July or August there were amendments. I think the first time I was asked was in September. I was asked to provide a rough sketch so that I could speak to Mr. Stefane when he came to Sarajevo, or perhaps it was in October. I can't provide you with an exact date now. And then all these shortcomings, errors were removed, corrections were made and then 15 or 20 days later Stefane would come to Sarajevo again and more corrections were made, and we continued to work in this way until we established the date, the 17th of December. And then by February of this year the final version was to be provided. I amended my report three or four times, at least. Added to it. Transformed certain thoughts, et cetera, et cetera. The work that requires continual effort, it's necessary to focus on such work, to ensure that the report satisfies certain criteria.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: An General, when you make reference in your last answer to Mr. Stefane, or Stefane, you're in fact referring to Mr. Bourgon, are you not?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you recall, sir, -- can you recall, General, in what way the questions were amended? Or do you have, perhaps, a copy of the original questions that you were asked?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have nothing here apart from my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you have any recollection as to how the questions were amended or how they evolved over time, if you can just give us some general -- a general overview or specifics, if you can recall specific examples.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for example, in the case of mobilisation, I would set up how the rules governed mobilisation in the JNA and, as usual, I prepared this in a very broad and general sense and then it was necessary to whittle it down. And I think that I provided about 200 pages. The report I provided consisted of about 200 pages and then I had to cut it down to down to 130 or 150 pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I take it, sir, from this answer that the questions were amended in such a way so that you could focus your attention and, thus, reduce the length of your report? Is that a fair overall summary?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, roughly speaking, that would be my viewpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would like to turn your attention and our focus now, sir, to the accused General Enver Hadzihasanovic. In order to prepare your report, it was necessary for you to gather some information about the professional experience and background of General Hadzihasanovic. Isn't that the case?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, how you went about doing that? What were the sources of that information, who you spoke to, or what documents you reviewed, in terms of reaching conclusions about the experience and professional background of General Hadzihasanovic?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was simply not necessary for me to consult anyone. I knew everything, but perhaps I had to consult someone to make sure that I hadn't made any mistakes when it came to his biography. Perhaps I had to consult Mustafa Polutak, et cetera, because I knew at least 90 per cent of Mr. Hadzihasanovic's biography from before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. General, you indicate in paragraph 345 of your report that General Hadzihasanovic did not complete what the English translation says Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. is "the JNA school for generals." And I'm wondering if you can give me the formal name of that school or academy.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the name is school of war. Perhaps General Hadzihasanovic will laugh. The war academy or the school of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Clearly there are a number of different military schools and academies at various levels. To the best of your recollection, the academy that would be the school or the training ground for promotion to the rank of general within the JNA was called the school of war, or the war academy?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's correct. If not, it's something like that. The name resembles that name.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you ever attend that school yourself?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, you told us that you knew about at least 90 per cent of General Hadzihasanovic's biography from before. Where did that 90 per cent that you knew from before come from? Where did that knowledge that you had about his background come from?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well we spent four or five months together in the course of the summer of 1992. We slept in the same place, in the operation centre every day, in the General Staff of the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you, sir: If you were aware or if you can confirm some of the following information about General Hadzihasanovic's professional background. Were you aware, sir, or did you know that he had commanded a military police company in the JNA from 1975 to 1980?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether he was in command of a military police company, but he was in command of a military police battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. That actually came later. But he was, in fact, the commander of a military police battalion in the JNA, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And do you know if, prior to that, he had been the deputy commander of a military police battalion? And prior to that, he'd been commander of a military police company?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We consider everything below the level of battalion to be unimportant, so I can't remember. Had I wanted to, I could have remembered that and I could have had such precise information, but I cannot now claim whether he was or wasn't, and what he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you know, sir, that he'd also commanded a motorised brigade in the city of Sarajevo immediately prior to the outbreak of the war?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was a mechanised brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you remember which brigade it was?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Lukavac brigade which is based in Lukavica in the immediate vicinity of the town of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Which is at Lukavica barracks?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Which we heard much about during the Galic trials, I'm sure you will appreciate. Let me ask you this, sir: You've told us, again on Monday, the 21st of March, that you first met General Hadzihasanovic in June or July of 1992. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.
