utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: There's a reference in the transcript on the 24th of March, 2005, that I believe is unclear and I'm going to ask you this so that we can clarify what I think is a discrepancy in the transcript. Because on page 14 of the transcript of 24 March, 2005, at lines 22, 23, the transcript says, quoting yourself, General: "I know General Hadzihasanovic from the JNA." And my question is: Did you actually know him during the time the both of you were in the JNA, or did you only meet him later?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I knew him personally at the time that the JNA existed, but I had heard of him. Perhaps that's why some confusion has arisen. I didn't personally know General Hadzihasanovic at the time the JNA existed but I had heard about him. I think the first time we actually met each other tete-a-tete was in fact in June or perhaps in July 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Then you told us, sir, in the autumn of 1992, when you were appointed the deputy commander of the 1st Corps, General Hadzihasanovic was the Chief of Staff of the 1st Corps of the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And as such, you were his immediate superior? Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our superior was the corps commander, but more or less it would be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And in late 1993, following the time period General Hadzihasanovic commanded the 3rd Corps, he was appointed Chief of Staff of the Main Staff of the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you describe for us, sir, what type of professional relationship, if any, existed between the Chief of Staff of the Main Staff, and the commander of the 1st Corps, that is, the position that you yourself held in late 1993?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The corps commander was directly subordinated in the chain of command to the commander of the General Staff of the BiH army. In terms of the relationship, the Chief of Staff of the General Staff, which was General Hadzihasanovic's position, did not have anything to do with corps commanders. In that respect, there is no subordination relationship. However, there is a line of operative work, a line of cooperation, between the General Staff and the corps staff. The Chief of Staff of the General staff, which was Hadzihasanovic's position, is in some -- in some way was subordinated to my Chief of Staff. However, this was not a chain of command and it was not strict subordination. This was professional subordination or operative subordination. I don't know whether I was clear enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you, sir, in a more direct way: Was General Hadzihasanovic, at the time he was Chief of Staff of the Main Staff of the ABiH at the end of 1993, your superior?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My superior was the commander of the General Staff of the BiH army, and I reported directly to him on all the issues which prevailed in my corps. The commander of the General Staff of the BiH army had his deputy, who was either Jovo Divjak or Siber, or so on and so forth. The Chief of Staff was the third or even the fourth person in that chain. General Hadzihasanovic, as the chief of the General Staff, if you are looking at that as a whole body, the whole General Staff and its function as the Chief of Staff, in a certain way he was my superior. However, it was not in the true military sense that he was my superior. Save for, in those situations, when the commander was absent and when his deputy was absent, there could be a very short interval during which the commander of the General Staff could authorise him to act on his behalf and to issue orders to the corps commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I note the time. It might be a few minutes early, but I would respectfully ask that we take our second technical break at this point in time. I will also inform the Chamber and my learned colleagues that I do anticipate that we will be completed with our cross-examination by the conclusion of today's court day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're going to make a break. It is 20 past 5.00 and we will resume around ten to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: General, I'm going to turn now to a few questions that I have concerning the accused Brigadier Amir Kubura. And you told us earlier this afternoon that you knew Brigadier Kubura from prior to the war and I would ask you some follow-up questions about that. I believe you told us that he was the commander of the 1st Muslim Brigade of the 1st Corps. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A. I don't know if I said that I knew him from before the war. I don't know whether I said that. And as for the second part of your question, the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask you this, then, General, so that we're very clear: Do you recall when was the first time, if ever, that you've met Amir Kubura face to face?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this was during the war. When I met him for the first time I wouldn't know. I can't be sure of the time. In any case, I heard of him when he was in the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade. And when he was reassigned to the 1st Corps of the BiH army, I believe that by then I had already seen him several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. And sir, can you tell us approximately when it was that Amir Kubura was reassigned to the ABiH 1st Corps?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this was in March 1994. I'm not sure though.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, you told us that you had heard of him when he was in the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade. Do you recall what you might have heard of him when he had commanded that brigade?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing special. I heard of many officers in the 5th Corps. I heard of many of them and I did not see many of them until the end of the war or even after the end of the war. So I can't say that it was either positive or negative. I just heard of him. I don't know whether I saw him first in Zenica when we went there for our debriefing. I don't know. I can't be sure of that. In any case, I'm sure that I met him before he before he joined my corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, I believe there might be an error in the transcript. Page 56, line 14, which should be on the screen in front of you. I would ask you if you could read that line to yourself and if you have anything that you want to correct about page 56, line 14 I would invite you to do so.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shall I correct myself?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If there is anything that is incorrect about page 56, line 14, I would invite you to tell us.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see a mistake there. I don't know what I'm supposed to correct, as much as I can read English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I asked you, sir, if you recall what you might have heard of him when he had commanded that brigade, referring to Brigadier Amir Kubura and the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade and you said: "Nothing special. I heard of many officers in the 5th Corps." Was the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade part of the 5th Corps?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I just mentioned the 5th Corps by way of example. The 5th Corps, throughout the war, was cut off from the main body of the BiH army, so I heard of many officers from the 5th Corps and I did not see many of them until the end of the war. And I mentioned the 5th Corps only by way of example.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, in order to produce your report and the section or the paragraphs that relate to Brigadier Kubura and the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, can you tell us, sir, what material you reviewed concerning the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Materials, documents, everything that has been recorded and that was registered by this Tribunal. Everything that is here behind me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, in your report -- again paragraph 477. My learned colleague, Mr. Ibrisimovic, asked you some questions about that paragraph. I would ask you if you could, please, to turn to paragraph 477. And I'm specifically interested, sir, in the last two sentences of that paragraph that begin with the phrase "On 12 March 1993". Do you see that sentence, sir?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You go on to write: "Brigadier Kubura was appointed Chief of Staff by the SVK." Did you see a document dated 12 March 1993 that appointed Brigadier Kubura Chief of Staff of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. If you're referring to the 12th of March, I don't know why. But in any case, I mentioned that in my report based on the document that I had at my disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, General Karavelic, do you have that document with you in the courtroom, in one of the binders behind you perhaps?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this document has been registered here with the Court, it should be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you, sir, if you can take a moment to see if it's in one of the binders behind you, the 12 March 1993 document. Perhaps with the assistance of the usher, if that document could be placed on the ELMO. Is that the document, sir, that you relied upon? Perhaps if the usher could move that up just a little bit up or perhaps zoom out. That's fine. Stop, please. Sir, is this in fact the document that you relied upon in reaching the conclusion that Brigadier Kubura was appointed Chief of Staff on the 12th of March, 1993?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please -- I believe it is under number 2, in the first section, can you read out that sentence relating to Mr. Kubura.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 477, my paragraph 477?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No, sir. In the document. The reference in the document to Mr. Kubura.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under 2: Kubura Nazifa Amir, born 4 March 1964. To the establishment post of the Chief of Staff and at the same time deputy commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So, sir, based on this document that you have before you, Brigadier Kubura was appointed Chief of Staff of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade and, at the same time, deputy commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Mountain Brigade. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, in your report at paragraph 477, there is no reference to him being appointed deputy commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade at the same time he was appointed Chief of Staff of that brigade. Is that right? Your report doesn't mention that fact.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is true. But it went without saying, because it is the document that is important. In -- and my expert report is not important in that sense. In my thinking, this was understood. But in any case it is the way you have said it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, General, you testified in response to some earlier questions and having had reference to the Rules of Service of the ABiH, and I would like to ask you if you could repeat for us the role of a deputy commander of a brigade when the commander of the brigade is absent.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there is a deputy commander, as a separate position, unlike in this case of Amir Kubura, if they are two persons, one who is the Chief of Staff and the other who is the deputy commander, then it is the deputy commander who acts on behalf of the brigade commander in his absence. In the spirit of my answer given to Mr. Ibrisimovic's question, since these two positions are held by one person, one officer, then this also arises in the second case. In the first case, however, if the deputy is the one who acts on behalf of the commander, then it is logical that in addition to acting in respect of one of his establishment posts, he also acts in respect of another establishment post which is the brigade commander. In the second cases, the two positions were held by one person, which was Amir Kubura. It would not have made any sense for him to act in respect of another position on top of the two positions that he already held.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you this, though, and let's focus on the situation as it existed in the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade in the time period March/April 1993, so that we're clear that's what we're talking about. As of the 12th of March 1993 Amir Kubura was appointed Chief of Staff and deputy commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade. True?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I didn't understand your question. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Based, sir, on the document that you have to your right on the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. projection machine, on the 12th of March, 1993 Sefer Halilovic, on behalf of the Supreme Command Staff, appointed Amir Kubura to be Chief of Staff and deputy commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, and as you put in your report, on the 6th of August, 1993, there is a different document which appoints Amir Kubura to be the commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, during the period between 12 March 1993 and 6 August 1993, when Brigadier Kubura was the Chief of Staff and deputy commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, during that time period, 12 March through 6 August 1993, when the commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, Asim Koricic, was not able to perform his duties as commander, who would be commanding the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Yugoslav People's Army all the rules say as follows: The brigade commander or the corps commander, it really doesn't matter what the unit level is, every commander commands his unit no matter where he is. I apologise for saying this, but just to illustrate this. The commander can be on the moon, abroad, in his own country, anywhere outside his brigade, he still remains its commander. There are several ways how the command and control role can be exercised. It can be through one's presence, or in the absence of that particular person, via telephone, via fax communication and so on and so forth. These are all the ways how the control and command function can be exercised. And this person remains in the position until the moment he is either relieved or abandons his duty in another way. This was the case in the JNA. I was in the situation on a number of occasions when my superior was not in Ljubljana and I was the battalion commander in Ljubljana. I did something on his behalf. He would ask me, Why you did that? No matter where I am, I'm still the commander, and you're not supposed to do anything on my behalf if I don't tell you to do that. For practical reasons, I'm telling you how it was in the JNA. For somebody not to be a commander, he has to be officially relieved of his duties by his superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I completely understand what you're saying, sir, but the fact is, during a wartime situation, if the commander is killed, taken prisoner of war, or simply flees the country, someone has to be in command at all times. Would you agree with that as a matter of principle?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're absolutely right. But, we're talking about a certain period, the period that I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes. I'm, again, focussing on the period between the 12th of March and the 6th of August, 1993, when Amir Kubura was formally appointed the commander and Asim Koricic was formally relieved of command as the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade. During that period, between the 12th of March and the 6th of August, 1993, if Asim Koricic left Bosnia and went to a third country, whether it was with permission or without permission, Amir Kubura was responsible for exercising command authority over the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade. Do you agree with that or not?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't fully agree with what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Again, let me put this as a hypothetical to you. Between the 12th of March and the 6th of August, 1993, the commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, the formally designated commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, leaves Bosnia and does not return prior to the end of the war. Does that person, who is outside of Bosnia, they might retain the formal position of commander until they are relieved, but in their absence someone must be in command of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is close to being the case, but it cannot be completely so because it goes against the things that I explained to you, in terms of what the procedure is, if that is the case. Then one might ask the question, why the order was issued on the first of August -- that is on the 6th of August, 1993, why was it that the order was issued at that moment, because that situation could have continued without the order. But it couldn't continue for several reasons. This should have been done at a much sooner and certainly no later than two months after the departure of the brigade commander. The order that was issued in August should have been issued earlier, appointing Amir Kubura to the position of the brigade commander and giving him the authority. I apologise. If Amir Kubura were to ask for his legal entitlements that arise from the position of the commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade for the period from the 12th of March to the 6th of August, he would not be able to exercise those rights, because legally he was not in that position at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That is most likely the case, sir. But my point is simply that during that period someone had to be in command of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade. In the absence of the commander, if he's gone, someone must be in charge.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally speaking you're absolutely right because the brigade is a living organism. A brigade are people. It is not a vehicle that you can just turn the engine off and you abandon it in the middle of the road. You have to work with people. And obviously what Amir Kubura did was what was supposed to be done and he did it and continued doing it. However, if I had been in his shoes, I would have pestered my superior and I would insist on him dealing with my status. I would have wanted things to be legal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, let me put to you, sir, that Asim Koricic left Bosnia on April 1st, meaning that the two-month period would have expired on June 1st, 1993. And in the event, in the event Mr. Kubura began pestering his commander to raise this issue with the Supreme Command Staff, that during the first two weeks of June 1993 the 3rd Corps commander might have been preoccupied with events going on in the Bijela valley. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not study other reasons why this was the case, why wasn't Brigadier Kubura appointed. However, what you have just mentioned may be part of the reasons. But I can't be sure of that. Because I don't know what was the key reason for which Amir Kubura was not appointed, either the acting commander or the commander, immediately by way of an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But again, sir, my only point is: Between the 12th of March and the 6th of August, 1993, if the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade commander left Bosnia, Amir Kubura as the deputy commander would be the de facto commander of that brigade.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may give you an assumption, a hypothetical situation. I'm not saying for a moment that this was indeed the case. This was just a hypothetical situation. Kubura already held a certain establishment position in that same brigade. He had his tasks and duties that arose from the position to which he had been appointed. I don't want to go through the list of all of these tasks and duties. Now the time came for him to do something else, a third set of duties, because there was nobody else to take them over. However, if I had been in his shoes, I would have perhaps thought that this same brigade commander could have contacts with other officers in my brigade with battalion commanders. How was I supposed to be sure that he didn't have such contacts? There was no way for me to be sure of that. And I'm just assuming that. This is just a hypothetical situation. But this assumption suffices. I could give you some other hypothetical thoughts which compel a person to do things as best as he can. This was the time of war and it would have been really bad if Amir Kubura had said, I don't want to lead this brigade. He would have transpired as a coward who didn't have the courage to lead his men. He probably did ask for his status to be resolved and it wasn't done. What could he have done in that position? In his shoes, what would I have done? Maybe I would have insisted even more on my requests being resolved. But it still remains questionable whether this would have been done. The time went on. The brigade had to live, it had to perform his duties. I'm just trying to look at the situation from the military point of view. And as for the legal weight of a certain situation, I cannot go into that. It is not my place to be the judge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to move on, General. But my point was precisely, I believe, what you were trying to make at the end, that is from a military point of view, leaving aside all the legal niceties, from a purely military point of view, someone is always in command of every unit.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Broadly speaking that conclusion is correct. That there are many other arguments that we must bear in mind, and I could pose the following question if I may. Why was it only on the 6th of August that Amir Kubura was appointed as brigade commander? And what if up until the 6th of August, 1993, the General Staff or corps commander didn't think that he was mature enough or capable to be the brigade commander. What if they thought he wasn't up to the task. What if that was the reason and he wasn't appointed as brigade commander until the 6th of August? But it turns out that he was de facto the brigade commander, and he was responsible for the brigade and the reason for which he wasn't appointed as brigade commander was, perhaps, the fact that someone assessed that he wasn't up to the task of commanding a brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me move on. Paragraph 477, the final sentence of your report, you write in reference to 6 August 1993: "Before this date, he had served as an acting commander of the brigade." My question to you, sir, is: When did he start serving as an acting commander of the brigade prior to the 6th of August 1993?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From a legal point of view, according to my assessment, according to my understanding, this could only have been during the first two months which was covered by the rules of service. And afterwards, he wasn't legally covered.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. And what period are you talking about when you say in your report he had served as an acting commander of the brigade? What time period are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well I'm referring to the two months, from the 1st of April and onwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what do you base that on? What material have you reviewed or what person you consulted with? What do you base that on?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's based on documents that don't state otherwise and it's based on the rules of service in the JNA. I didn't find any documents that stated the contrary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me move on to some general points with respect to your report. In paragraph 499, I'd ask you if you could, sir, to please turn to paragraph 499. Let me ask you, sir -- do you have paragraph 499 in front of you?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You write in this or paragraph sir, and I'm quoting: "The only way to assess how both commanders reacted to certain events during this period is to look at what happened through their eyes, taking into consideration the prevailing circumstances at the time." This would seem, General, to imply that a subjective and not an objective approach is taken by yourself, in terms of writing this report.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I wrote this -- I'll provide you with another example. I meant that if I had been in Amir Kubura's position, or rather I asked myself, If I had been in Amir Kubura's position, what would I have done? And I said I would probably have done something very similar, if not exactly the same thing. If I had been the Chief of Staff or the deputy, which was Kubura's case, and my brigade commander left, then as the next most senior officer, I would have had to perform my duties. I wouldn't have had the right to sit down and say the brigade's life will now end because I would then have suffered other legal consequences. The life and the activities of the brigade must continue. If I had said I won't perform these duties, and if I abandoned the duties I had been assigned, I would have suffered far more serious legal consequences. I couldn't do this. All I could do is act as Kubura did, to continue working and to ask, at the same time, to have my status regulated, because he had no other solution. He had no better solution. As to why they waited until the 6th of August, 1993 to resolve the matter, that's something I can't comment on. That's another matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I appreciate, General, that answer, but I have moved on to part 4 of your report and my question is a more general one, based on what you wrote in paragraph 499. And my question is, to the extent you can render your opinion on this as the author of the report, did you take a subjective approach, that is, viewing the events as they happened through the eyes of the two accused? Or did you attempt to take an objective approach?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even now I ask myself how I could have assessed this differently. As to whether I was being more subjective or more objective, I don't know. All I can say, that I really tried to avoid being subjective. I don't know whether I fully succeeded in doing that. Someone else should say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But in paragraph 499 you state: "In my opinion, the only way to assess how both commanders reacted is to look at what happened through their eyes." And so my question isn't so much whether your report is objective, but whether the methodology that you used relates to taking a subjective approach, based on what you wrote in paragraph 499.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if there's some confusion with regard to the term, but in this paragraph I wanted to refer to all the events that took place. When I said to look at things through their eyes, that means placing myself in their position, in their shoes during that period of time, in order to have the best possible understanding of the situation at that period of time, during that period of time. And in the belief that that would enable me to be as objective as possible, because I wanted to depict the reality and all the difficulties that existed at that time, that caused all the commanders at all levels very serious problems. That was my purpose. However, if one claims that the methodology appears to be a subjective methodology, well, that is not something I would agree with.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Mundis. It's 20 to 7.00 now. Will Defence counsel prefer to wait until tomorrow for their re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. With the Chamber's leave we would rather wait until tomorrow to commence our examination. I think I will need an hour and a half and it would be preferable to start tomorrow so as to avoid breaking up our re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We will then continue with your re-examination tomorrow. We will now adjourn, but before we do so, General, you should be back in the courtroom at 9.00 tomorrow morning. The hearing will be held in the morning tomorrow at 9.00. I invite everyone to return for the hearing at 9.00 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
